title: Model 1 — scored governance assessment (output)
description: The engine's assessment of a single issue: five scored dimensions, a priority tier and a next action.

score.description: Ordinal scale. Compound values are permitted where the rubric genuinely straddles two anchors; they are treated as the lower value for tier derivation.

id.description: Identifier of the issue assessed, where the input carried one.

evidence_strength.description: How directly and how well corroborated the evidence is. Low: inference from secondary material. Moderate: direct but partial or single-source. High: direct, corroborated, method documented.

chronology_clarity.description: How clearly the sequence is established. Low: periods unclear or contested. Moderate: sequence known, some gaps. High: dated sequence established end to end.

governance_relevance.description: Bearing on transparency, assurance and accountability. Low: peripheral. Moderate: bears on one control objective. High: goes directly to transparency, assurance or accountability.

operational_impact.description: Consequence for auditability and assurance posture. Low: no effect. Moderate: affects confidence in one domain. High: affects auditability or assurance maturity broadly.

actionability.description: Whether the issue can be acted on. Low: no owner, no lever, no forum. Moderate: reviewable, remedy unclear. High: clear owner, clear next step, defined forum. Scored independently of the other four.

priority_tier.description: Derived from the scores by the tier rules; not assigned directly.

next_action.description: The specific next step, naming a forum or owner where one exists.

rationale.description: Optional note on why the tier fell where it did, particularly where a compound score decided it.
